clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 13294 sec. 2 ('Executive Order 11157 of June 22, 1964, as amended, and Executive Order 11800 of August 17, 1974, as amended, are hereby revoked'); EO 13294 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, March 28, 2003 (printed 68 FR 15919, April 1, 2003)
clauses.reason: Whole order (sec. 1 delegation of the President's functions under 37 U.S.C. 301a to the Secretaries of Defense, Transportation for the Coast Guard, Commerce and Health, Education, and Welfare for uniformed-service members under their jurisdictions; sec. 2 effective as of 1974-06-01, a one-time effective-date rule). Ended by the revocation in EO 13294 sec. 2, effective on signing, 2003-03-28. Partial amendments before the revocation changed names only and left the delegation in force: EO 12608 sec. 15 (signed 1987-09-09, replaced the Department and Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare by Health and Human Services) and EO 13286 sec. 58 (replaced the Secretary of Transportation by the Secretary of Homeland Security, effective 2003-03-01 under its sec. 92). EO 13294 sec. 1 re-delegates the same 37 U.S.C. 301a authority, with 301 and 301c, to the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Health and Human Services and Homeland Security.

savings.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_13294 (EO 13294, 68 FR 15917-15919, read once in full): sec. 1 designates the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Health and Human Services and Homeland Security (for the Coast Guard) to exercise, without presidential approval, the authority under 37 U.S.C. 301, 301a and 301c; sec. 2 revokes EO 11157 and EO 11800; sec. 3 is a no-private-rights clause; there is no savings, pending-matter or exception clause. The held file also prints the preceding order, EO 13293, whose sentence 'Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the exercise of authority granted by Executive Order 12776' belongs to that order, not to EO 13294. Own-residual check, reading EO 11800 in full: it delegated the President's 37 U.S.C. 301a functions (aviation career incentive pay) to named Secretaries. That delegation of function is carried forward by EO 13294 sec. 1 to the same officials, with wider reach, and aviation career incentive pay already entitled under it is an accrued benefit; nothing in EO 13294 ends either. Bounded search: EO 11800 and EO 13294 in full, plus the amending provisions of EO 12608 sec. 15 and EO 13286 sec. 58.

research_rationale: EO 11800 (signed August 17, 1974; 39 FR 30103), read in full from the held FR text, delegates the President's functions under 37 U.S.C. 301a (Aviation Career Incentive Act of 1974) and is effective as of June 1, 1974. It has no term or sunset. EO 13294 (signed March 28, 2003; 68 FR 15917-15919), read in full, revokes it with EO 11157 in sec. 2 and states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. The U.S. Code note at 37 U.S.C. 301a note records the amendments by EO 12608 and EO 13286 sec. 58 and the revocation by EO 13294. The dossier holds no located ACT record for EO 12608 and its record for EO 13286 is an American Presidency Project transcription, so both amendments are described in the clause reason (read in the held official FR texts, EO_12608.txt sec. 15 list and EO_13286.txt sec. 58) rather than attached as later events; neither ended anything. The dossier's single scope covers the whole operative text (secs. 1-2). Earlier-end test: the OFR catalog hits (4), U.S. Code and eCFR hits (4 each) show only those two amendments and the revocation. The 1989 Codification lead is an editorial snapshot and is not used as a legal basis.
